attrs.text:
Looking @docs/design/Task-Classification-thoughts.md and the master arch doc @docs/design/coding-econ-design-draft.md few things I want to clarify and think thru carefully.
  - What are the essential events. session_id, user_id, model, time etc. that are tables stakes and must be there. These common event structure will expand.
  - While reading classification design I realized a coding agent deals with files of all types, code files, documents (md, pdf, word), configs, databases etc. These are READ and many are WRITTEN/edited via tools. So not having tool input param maynot be right idea at all. I actually said to do that since I thought classifier doesn't need input files in order to signfy type of task. However in order to track output as well as finely classify it is important to know types of file and data. 
  - We need to know what files are being edited and produced to track git commits as well. 

So I beleive the design should have the input parameters of tools in the event msg. The classifier can ignore that

Think about and answer. Provide reasons

Mostly agree and thinking thru. I also meant meta params, not the raw lines of EDIT but the filepath. 
If type derivation is via extension there is not need to figure that out localy. If the type of file needss a bit more input for classification, like headers of a file or not then there is option to do it locally vs. at the server. Server could be faster and more importantly I want to minimize processing on the local end. At this moment we don't think we need anythng beyond filepath, repo_name, lines added/removed etc. 
- The signals for overlap would need block of line in the file. I would think so. 
- MCP server is an interesting case. I don't think I made any call reagarding that. As of this desing it will have the MCP server name correct. In that case it should be added in a section that needs further thought. 
- The arch. block shows P3 is processing block. Yes but there will variety of processing each requiring different CPU and memory profile. It certainly not going to be single process, possibley multiple dockerized containers. The classifiers would be its own process. That distinction needs to clearly marked in the arch doc.
- Task classification and associated cost, latency etc. now is part of phase-1. So revise that in arch doc. 


Now lets talk about the shape of the event msg.
 You are using a terminoology called envelope and type specific data. I am from networking protocol background. We often create event structures as
  - Headers: Envelop, alwasy present in every msg. This would also evolve but the struture starts with mandotory Header. 
 .- Optional Field: Within Optionfield it is an array of TLV,often refered as Type length value. Essentialy in this case they could be array of JSON. 
The distinction of HEADER + OPTIONAL is important arcitectural pattern that needs to be reflected in the arch document. 

Your opinion as sr architect.

questions.question: How should the schema be notated in the doc?

options.label: Annotated JSON skeleton (Recommended)
options.description: A JSON block where each field's value states its type and constraint. Crisp and readable in a design doc; the pydantic models in code become the normative machine schema.

options.label: Formal JSON Schema
options.description: A real JSON Schema (draft 2020-12) document with type/required/enum keywords. Machine-precise but verbose — roughly 3–4x longer for the same information.

options.label: Skeleton + formal schema file
options.description: Annotated skeleton in the doc for readability, plus a commitment that a versioned JSON Schema file in the repo (generated from the pydantic models) is the normative contract.

questions.question: How much of the payload (type-specific) structures should be fully spelled out in the doc?

options.label: Every event type, fully (Recommended)
options.description: One JSON structure per event type (session_start, user_message, assistant_message, tool_call, sub_agent_spawn, file_change, session_end, git_event, plan_usage_snapshot). Longest, but the contract is complete in one place — matches 'this part must be crisp'.

options.label: Header + tool_call fully, table for the rest
options.description: Full JSON for the header and the tool_call payload (the most complex and the one we debated); the remaining payload types as a compact field table.

questions.question: Field naming convention on the wire?

options.label: snake_case (Recommended)
options.description: event_id, parent_id, cache_read_tokens. Matches Python/pydantic and Postgres column names — zero translation layers server-side.

options.label: camelCase
options.description: eventId, parentId. Matches the vendor JSONL files being normalized (e.g. Claude Code's parentUuid) and common JSON API style, but needs mapping to Python/Postgres names.

questions.question: Is the three-part split literal nesting on the wire, or logical grouping over a flat object?

options.label: Literal nesting (Recommended)
options.description: The event is physically { "header": {...}, "payload": {...}, "ext": {...} }. The contract is self-evident in every sample event, and the header→columns / payload→JSONB storage split maps one-to-one.

options.label: Flat object, logical grouping
options.description: All fields at one level; header vs payload is documentation convention. A few bytes smaller and flatter to query, but the mandatory/optional boundary is invisible in the data itself.

Ok One small change.
Our nitial proof point with customers would with existing jsonl files. That means a -batch mode. 
The adapter simply processes the whole available file. 
However lets keep it in a way that normalizer gets some chunks and processes as it is being streamed. Want to keep the same pipleline.

ok Lets go back to the Task Classification design @docs/design/Task-Classification-thoughts.md, I have added some notes @docs/design/notes/coding_agent_task_classification_framework.md 
I have done similar work befre so i want explore the DAG callgraph of tools in a given task.

- For classification purpose.
- Can we use that to identify rework. 
- Can this work as better classifire. But if it needs more data and labeling then it is not the starting point.
- Can this identify potential anomalies. What kind

I want your thougtful opinion

Your explanation often tends to be pedantic and I loose it. Try to be less pedantic and more direct next time. SO let me rephrase what I undersood from your ananlysis.
1. The graph is very useful. Not so much for classification but for motif. Explain motif to me. I view is as behvior of task. 
2. the graph could be very useful in sub-labels. 
3. The signals for rework, no progress etc. are now can actually be measured. 

I have other observations, but before that lets make sure we understand each other. Be consice.

Ok lets use the behavior, we understand it better. A terminology like motif is not widely used in anomalies or behavorial analysis. 

Now the Tier0 requires signatures. Whow will provide it? Seems like those are config driven. 
If so it would make the deployments complicated. 
A review folder has reviews
A doc folde has documents. 
Well those are generally inferred by human as sunch, no signatures required. The key is that this has to be supplied by us, not by customeers. They may expand it but must not bear the burden of providing it to use this.

2) Tier 1 : local ML. vs. cheap model doing a zero shot intent classification. I would do cheap LLM classification, perhaps improve with caching etc. rather than ML. For proto both cost and latency is negligible. local ML is something for optimizing cost and latency later.

options.description: Each task shows exact file paths, interface signatures, test names with assertions spelled out, run commands with expected output — but no implementation bodies. Honors your 'no code' instruction; implementer writes the bodies via TDD.
options.preview:

options.label: Full code per skill
options.description: Complete test code and implementation code in every step, per the writing-plans standard. Most detailed, but it is literally writing the codebase inside markdown — very long docs, and contradicts your earlier 'no code whatsoever' instruction.

questions.question: Which scope do I plan at full task granularity now?

options.label: M0–M1 detailed now, rest at milestone start (Recommended)
options.description: One detailed plan for the backfill proof point (skeleton + contract + collector backfill → ingest → sessions/cost), ~25–35 tasks. M2–M5 get a roadmap doc now and their own detailed plan when reached — plans written months ahead of execution go stale.

options.label: All milestones detailed now
options.description: Six detailed plan docs covering M0–M5 (~100+ tasks total). Complete picture up front; M3–M5 details will likely need rewriting by the time you get there.
